The manipulation of time in the story is well-balanced and serves the character development effectively. The author appropriately uses **compression of time** to summarize long periods that establish routine, background, or gradual evolution—such as compressing twelve years of cashier work into a single paragraph, summarizing an eight-month courtship into a few sentences, and condensing the "first year of marriage" into a brief overview of "small surrenders." Conversely, the narrative slows down to allow pivotal scenes with Miss Emily—such as their first meeting, the wedding toast, the tour of the company, and the dinner confrontation—to unfold in real-time through dialogue and detailed internal reflection. This rhythm allows the story to cover roughly fifteen years of Nell's life while maintaining a tight, emotional focus on the crucial moments that define her relationship with her mother-in-law and her own sense of identity.
